question: A dealer marked the price of an item 40% above its cost price. He allowed two successive discounts of 25% and 16% to a particular customer. As a result, he incurred a loss of Rs. 590 . At what price did he sell the item to the said customer?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let CP = 100

SP = 140% × 75% × 84% = 88.2

Loss (100 - 88.2) units = 590

11.8 units = 590

1 units = 50 

**∴ SP = 50 × 88.2 = Rs. 4410**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

The dealer marked the price of an item 40% above its cost price. 

He allowed two successive discounts of 25% and 16% to a particular customer.

He incurred a loss of Rs. 590.

Concept used:

Final discount percentage after two successive discounts of A% and B% = (A + B - {AB over 100})\%

Selling Price = Cost Price - Loss

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Marked Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Rise%

Loss = Selling Price - Cost Price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the item be 100p.

It's marked price = 100p + 100p × 40% = 140p

Final resultant discount = 25 + 16 - (25 × 16)/100 = 37%

It's selling price = 140p - 140p × 37% = 88.2p

Loss incurred = 100p - 88.2p = 11.8p

According to the question,

11.8p = 590

⇒ p = 590/11.8

⇒ p = 50

Now, it's selling price = 88.2 × 50 = Rs. 4410

∴ He sold the item to the said customer at Rs. 4410.
